steps.body: Testing every interval is honest but slow. The shortcut (recall bounce vs cross): at an **odd-multiplicity** zero the sign **flips**; at an **even-multiplicity** zero it **doesn't**. Find ONE interval's sign, then walk the chart flipping only at odd zeros.
The multiplicity shortcut, in one picture.

widget.prompt: p(x) = (x + 3)x³(x − 2)². Set the signs. Watch the CUBED root carefully.
widget.successFeedback: + − + +. The cube at 0 is ODD, so it flips the sign just like a single root does — multiplicity 3 crosses, it merely flattens on the way through. The square at 2 is even, so it bounces and changes nothing. Only the parity matters.
widget.crossFeedback: An odd multiplicity — 1 or 3 — is a crossing. Both x = −3 and x = 0 must flip the sign.
widget.bounceFeedback: You flipped across x = 2, but that root is squared. Even multiplicity bounces off the axis and leaves the sign alone.

predict.prompt: p(x) = (x + 3)x³(x − 2)² cuts the line into four intervals. Before you set a single sign — how many of them are negative?

options.label: One — only the stretch between −3 and 0
Two — every root flips the sign as you pass it
One — but it is the far-left stretch, because a repeated root bounces

predict.reveal: One: the signs run + − + +. Parity decides. The cube at 0 is an ODD power, so it crosses — it only flattens on the way through — while the square at 2 is even and bounces, leaving the sign alone. A repeated root is not automatically a bouncing root.

cml.actionGoal: Set interval signs and use root multiplicity to explain where a function crosses or only touches the axis.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change the controlling quantity in this signChart away from the successful state. Which invariant remains true, and which visible consequence changes?

explanation.prompt: Why does an even root not reverse the interval sign?

options.label: The factor changes sign an even number of times, so the graph touches and returns to the same side.
options.feedback: Exactly—this identifies the governing mechanism rather than only the final pattern.

options.label: All roots force a crossing.
options.feedback: That describes an appearance or shortcut, not the invariant that makes the relationship hold.

options.label: Only the leading coefficient matters at every interval.
options.feedback: The live model contradicts that claim when its control is changed.

explanationVariants: x = 3 has multiplicity 2 — even — so NO flip: g stays positive just left of 3.
(x − 3)² can't change the product's sign; crossing 3 leaves g at +.

widget.prompt: Crossing the zero x = 3 (multiplicity 2) from right to left, the sign of g:

options.label: stays positive — even multiplicity, no flip
options.feedback: Right — the squared factor touches zero and bounces; the sign survives.

options.label: flips to negative
options.feedback: Flips happen at ODD multiplicity. The square (even) bounces: still +. Check g(0) = 9·2 = 18 > 0.

options.label: becomes zero on the whole interval
options.feedback: g is zero only AT x = 3; between zeros the sign is constant — here, still positive.

explanationVariants: x = −2 has multiplicity 1 — odd — so the sign FLIPS to negative left of −2. Chart: −, +, +.

widget.prompt: Continuing the walk across x = −2 (multiplicity 1), the full sign chart of g, left to right, is:

commonBuilds.feedback: That pattern flips at BOTH zeros — but x = 3 is even multiplicity and doesn't flip: −, +, +.
That flips at 3 instead of −2 — backwards: the odd zero is −2. The chart is −, +, +.

widget.missFeedback: Flip only at odd-multiplicity zeros: −2 flips, the even 3 does not.
widget.successFeedback: Right — flip at the odd zero −2, no flip at the even zero 3.

steps.body: Harvesting from −, +, +: g > 0 on (−2, 3) **and** (3, ∞) — but watch x = 3 itself: g(3) = 0, so for a **strict** inequality the point x = 3 is a **puncture** in an otherwise positive run.

explanationVariants: g > 0 everywhere right of −2 EXCEPT the single point x = 3, where g = 0: x > −2 with x ≠ 3.
Both + intervals join, minus the puncture at the bounce point.

commonBuilds.feedback: Almost — at x = 3 itself g = 0, which is not > 0. Puncture it: x > −2, x ≠ 3.
g(0) = 9 · 2 = 18 > 0 — the interval (−2, 3) is positive too. Only the single point 3 fails.

widget.missFeedback: The even zero never separates signs — it only punctures the strict inequality at the single point.
widget.successFeedback: Right — the even zero doesn't separate signs, but it IS a zero: strictly positive fails exactly there.

explanationVariants: Far right +; flip at 5 (odd) → −; no flip at −1 (even, exponent 2) → −. Chart: −, −, +. So h ≤ 0 on x ≤ 5, with the zero 5 included and −1 automatically included (h(−1) = 0).
h < 0 on both left intervals; adding equality pulls in the zeros −1 and 5: all of x ≤ 5.
hints: Start far right: sign of h for huge x?
Walk left: flip at the odd zero 5; then what happens at the even zero −1?
Chart −, −, +. For ≤ 0, harvest the − intervals plus every zero.

commonBuilds.feedback: h(0) = 1 · (−5) = −5 < 0: the negativity continues past −1 all the way to 5.
The far-left interval is negative too — check h(−2) = 1·(−7) = −7. All of x ≤ 5 works.

widget.missFeedback: The even zero at −1 brings no sign flip — negativity runs from far left up through 5, endpoints in.
widget.successFeedback: Right — both left intervals are negative (no flip at the even zero −1), and the zeros −1, 5 satisfy h = 0.

steps.body: Count the exponents, skip the tests.
takeaways: Odd multiplicity flips the sign; even doesn't.
Anchor one interval (far right is easiest), then walk.
Even zeros can puncture a strict-inequality solution.
steps.teaser: Next: solving inequalities that don't arrive pre-factored.

concept.body: Sign-walk recipe: pick the far-right sign from the leading coefficient, then moving left, flip at odd-multiplicity zeros only.

explanationVariants: Multiplicity 4 is even: no flip — the sign stays positive.
Even powers bounce; the chart keeps its + across x = 2.

widget.prompt: Walking a sign chart across a zero of multiplicity 4, the sign:

options.label: stays the same
options.feedback: Right — even multiplicity never flips the sign.

options.label: flips
options.feedback: Flips are for ODD multiplicities (1, 3, 5, …). Four is even: no flip.

options.label: flips twice
options.feedback: There's no double-flip — one crossing, one decision: even means unchanged.
